title: Harmonious construction of Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles

content.statement: Where possible, Part III and Part IV of the Constitution are to be interpreted so as to give effect to both, without ignoring Article 37's rule that Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts as rights.
elements: Avoid needless conflict between Part III and Part IV
content.development: Developed in Supreme Court jurisprudence on the relationship between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles; applied alongside basic structure limits on amendments.
content.application: Use when interpreting statutes that implement Directive Principles and are challenged under Part III, or when reading constitutional provisions together.
exceptions: Cannot create a freestanding Part IV cause of action
Cannot override clear Part III text without a valid constitutional basis such as a properly applicable savings clause
